resolution.note: hc host labels the successor herdr.space=<caller space> (else the space whose folder is the cwd, else herdr-app space.new), so it opens as a visible tab; regression tests on verbatim hc get t12 / herdr-app ls / space.new captures red 2 before, green after. Live probe 2026-11-15: an hc terminal labelled herdr.space showed as tab 2 of its space and hc kill removed that tab, so --retire (hc kill) already closes the predecessor's app tab. Disposition: closing a legacy Herdr TUI pane from an hc successor is not built: selectHost prefers HC_TERMINAL_ID and an hc terminal inherits the core's HERDR_* variables, so HERDR_PANE_ID in an hc terminal is not the predecessor's pane; that cross-host handoff only happens by hand.

title: A successor launched through hc opens as a visible tab in the Herdr desktop app
body:
Why: the hc host (src/successor/host-hc.ts:69-77) starts the successor with `hc run --bg --no-parent --cwd <cwd> --label krn-tab=<name>`; per `herdr-app --skill`, a terminal started with hc shows in the window only with `herdr.space=<id>` (and optionally `herdr.tab=<id>`), "unlabeled workers stay hidden". So a successor launched from a lead inside the Herdr desktop app runs invisibly; the operator cannot see or reach it. Observed 2026-11-15: the handoff into the app had to be done by hand with `herdr-app do space.new/tab.new`.
Outcome: the hc host labels the successor with the predecessor terminal's `herdr.space` (read from `hc get $HC_TERMINAL_ID` labels, else a space whose folder is the repository root, created with `herdr-app do space.new --name krn --folder <root>` when missing) so it opens as a visible tab; `--retire` closes the predecessor tab in the app too, and also closes a legacy Herdr (TUI) predecessor pane when HERDR_PANE_ID was handed over.
Proof: regression test on a verbatim `hc get` capture red before the fix; a live round trip shows the successor tab in `herdr-app ls`.
